description: Memory arms, NL: GPT-6 Astra on 5 mechanics-15 mazes under the R2 NL cell (run_config.mechanics_15_nl.json: minimal/text_only/egocentric/zero_shot/stateless, step_by_step, progress_stall_k=30, prompt caching on), memory arm scratchpad_window (a model-written scratchpad plus only the last 5 steps of history). One of three configs that differ only in the memory arm: run_config.mechanics_15_nl_memory_{full_context,scratchpad_window,full_context_scratchpad}.json.
_note_no_conditions: No conditions key => single (default) cell built from experiment_config overlay. Do NOT add conditions (that would re-enable the sweep).
_note_requires: The memory field comes from the scratchpad memory PR (interface/scratchpad.py); launching before it is on the launched SHA fails at config load for the two scratchpad arms.
_note_prompt: The R2 NL prompt with: one sentence after the Valid actions line of the system prompt ("Scratchpad: write notes between <scratchpad> and </scratchpad> in each reply; they replace your previous notes and are shown to you at the next step (at most 2000 characters)."); the history cut to the last 5 steps under "Recent history (last 5 steps, oldest first):" (the same per-step lines as the full history); the current notes after the current state ("Your scratchpad:" and the notes between the tags); the reply format opening with the <scratchpad> block before FINAL_OUTPUT.
_note_mazes: The 5 mazes where R2 NL Astra (full context, 15/15 solved) spent the most steps over the BFS optimum: M8 portals_frozen 168 vs 95, M8 death_frozen 195 vs 161, M10 (all four mechanics) 100 vs 75, M9 portals_death_frozen 103 vs 81, M8 frozen_rotating 161 vs 144. Together they cover portals, death, rotating and frozen tiles, and they are long (75-161 optimal steps), so a 5-step window drops most of the history.
_note_model_params: GPT-6 Astra exactly as in run_config.mechanics_15_nl.json (reasoning_effort=xhigh, flex tier, 64k max_completion_tokens, prompt caching on) except spend_cap_usd and worker concurrency. spend_cap_usd is a per-process hard stop (run each arm in its own process) and, like every runtime model key, enters the run hash, so these units do not reuse R2's cached episodes.
_note_cost: Projected from R2's measured episodes (same lengths) plus the notes: each query writes the notes as output ($25/M on flex) and reads them back uncached ($5/M). With 150 / 300 / 500 tokens of notes per query (500 is the 2,000-character cap): ~$10 / ~$14 / ~$18 for the 5 episodes, vs ~$7 at full context. Input is NOT cheaper than full context at these lengths: full context reads its history from cache at $0.50/M (R2: ~$2.59 input for the 5 episodes), while the 5-step window is resent uncached every query (~$3.3-4.6 with the notes). The window only saves input on long episodes; output (the notes) dominates either way. Worst case (every episode to its 3x step cap, 500-token notes every query): ~$41. spend_cap_usd=45.
_note_launch: Local run in its own artifacts root: the three arms share run directories (keyed by task/backend/model/seed/variant, not by arm), so one root would hold only the last arm run. Pre-score Stage 2 once (no model calls): python -m scripts.run_pipeline --distributed-role coordinator-prepare --run-config gridworld/fixtures/run_config.mechanics_15_nl_memory_scratchpad_window.json --manifest gridworld/fixtures/manifest.mechanics_15.json --seeds 0 --difficulty-max-static-score 8000 --artifacts-root artifacts-memory/prescored; then cp -r artifacts-memory/prescored/tasks artifacts-memory/scratchpad_window/ and run: python -m scripts.run_pipeline --run-config gridworld/fixtures/run_config.mechanics_15_nl_memory_scratchpad_window.json --manifest gridworld/fixtures/manifest.mechanics_15.json --seeds 0 --difficulty-max-static-score 8000 --artifacts-root artifacts-memory/scratchpad_window. Serial at ~11 s per Astra query on flex (R2 NL): about 2-3 hours for the 5 episodes; the three arms can run side by side as three processes.
_note_cache: full_context and full_context_scratchpad: the history goes out one text block per step with breakpoints on the newest step and the previous request's newest step, as in R2; the scratchpad sits after the last breakpoint with the current state, so the cached prefix is the same as full_context's. scratchpad_window: the window slides every step, so only the system prompt is cached.
